cover_hook: A spacecraft just used Earth to slingshot to Jupiter
caption_hook: 🚀 ESA's Juice spacecraft swung past Earth and gained 3.5 km/s on its way to Jupiter, using almost no fuel + 3 more wins you missed 👇
question: Space slingshot or Stone Age timbers: which would you rather see up close?
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves space
reel_hook: This spacecraft borrowed speed from Earth
first_comment: Bonus: Juice snapped photos of Earth as it passed just 8,640 km above the Indian Ocean. It'll swing by one last time in 2029 before reaching Jupiter in 2031. 🌍

stories.stat_label: km per second of free speed
stories.headline: ESA's Juice gains 3.5 km/s by swinging past Earth
stories.summary: Juice passed 8,640 km above Earth, and our planet's gravity bent its path by 20° and sped it up, using very little fuel. It's on its way to 35 flybys of Jupiter's icy moons.
stories.why: Saved fuel means more time studying moons that may hide oceans.

stories.headline: Melbourne puts out 100 'bricks' birds can build nests from
stories.summary: Made of bark, twigs, coconut fibre and moss, the bricks slowly break down so birds like fairy wrens can take natural material instead of plastic and cigarette butts.
stories.why: Litter has been found in the nests of 176 bird species.

stories.stat_label: years with no major forest fire
stories.headline: Village women kept their forest fire-free 3 years running
stories.summary: In Marhmanley, Himalayan women led by council head Kamla Devi plan small controlled burns and rush to put out sparks with branch brooms, so the village has avoided major blazes.
stories.why: About 95% of India's forest fires are started by people, so prevention works.

stories.headline: Divers find 10,500-year-old timbers at a lake bottom
stories.summary: Under 20 m of water, divers recovered a 1.6 m post with chop marks and split boards up to 1.3 m long, left by Stone Age hunter-gatherers. Wood this old almost never survives.
stories.why: They could be huts built 3,000 years before the first farmers' houses.

fun_fact: Juice will need 8 years and flybys of Earth and Venus to reach Jupiter.
